It has come in a hadith that when he, peace be upon him, put his foot in the stirrup he would say: "In the name of God," and when he settled upon the mount he would say: "Praise be to God for every state; glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and to Him we are returning," and he would say "Allahu akbar" three times and "La ilaha illa Allah" three times. They also said: when one boards a ship he says: "In the name of God is its course and its anchorage" up to "Merciful," and at disembarking one says: "O God, cause us to alight at a blessed landing place, for You are the best of those who cause to alight."

"Qarn" (ability): the one who is dominant, controlling, capable of a thing; it is said: "aqrana al-shay'," when he was able to manage it. Ibn Hermah said:
"You have made able what you laid upon me, and little is it that endurance bears the rejection and the forsaking, O Da'd."
The literal sense of "aqranahu" is that he found it a counterpart to himself, and that which is bound to it. For the difficult does not become a counterpart to the weak. The poet said:
"And the son of the camel-colt, when he is tied with a rope, cannot withstand the charge of the stout, long-necked camels."
"Qarn" is also the rope with which something is tied. Abu 'Ubayd said: "Fulan muqrin li-fulan," meaning he controls him. The meaning is that we have no strength to control the beast and the ship; it is God who subjected them. Qutrub recited for 'Amr ibn Ma'dikarib:
"Indeed the tribes know that 'Aqil, in our favour in the calamities, is not one who subdues us."
It was also read "lamuqtarinin," the active participle of "iqtarana."

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 43, verse 1–18 (part 3 of 3):

﴿And indeed, to our Lord we are returning﴾: i.e., returning (raji'un). This is an affirmation of the return to Allah and of the Resurrection (al-ba'th), because the rider is in a position of possible destruction by drowning when he boards a ship, and by being thrown from a mount, since riding an animal is a matter fraught with danger, and safety in it is not assured. So his saying this is a reminder that he is conscious of the eventual return to Allah and prepared to meet Him, and he does not leave that from his heart or his tongue.

﴿And they have made for Him﴾: i.e., the disbelievers of Quraysh and the Arabs have made for Him, i.e., for Allah, (min 'ibadihi) of His servants: i.e., from among those who are the servants of Allah, (juz'an), a portion. Mujahid said: a share and a lot, and this is the saying of the Arabs: "The angels are the daughters of Allah." Qatadah said: juz'an, i.e., a rival (nid), and that is the idols, Pharaoh, and whoever was worshipped besides Allah. It was also said: al-juz' means females. Some of the linguists said: it is said "ajza'at al-mar'ah" when she gives birth to a female. The poet said:
"If a free woman bears a female one day, there is no wonder, for a free woman sometimes bears a male."
It was said: this verse is fabricated, and likewise his saying:
"He married her to one of the daughters of al-Aws, one who bears females."

Since it had been mentioned that they acknowledge that He, the Exalted, is the Creator of the world, He rebuked them for making for Him a part, while they have acknowledged that He is the Creator. How then do they describe Him with an attribute of the created? ﴿Indeed, man is clearly ungrateful﴾ for the blessing of his Creator. (mubin): manifest in his denial. What is meant by "man" is the one who makes for Allah a part, and others among the disbelievers. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "mubin" in this place is intransitive. End of quote. It is not necessarily restricted to what he mentioned; rather, its meaning may be that it is apparent in ingratitude for blessings and manifest in his denial, as we have said.

﴿Has He taken daughters from what He creates?﴾: an interrogative of denial and rebuke for the scantiness of their intellects. How did they claim that He, the Exalted, took for Himself what you yourselves hate, when you yourselves, when news of them is brought to you, your faces darken, and you bury them alive? (wa-asfakum): He made for you the choicest of what is beloved, and that is sons. His saying (min ma yakhluqu) is an alert to the impossibility of offspring, whether male or female; and even if the taking of offspring is supposed, how would He choose for Himself the lesser and reserve the higher for you? He mentioned the daughters first because they are the ones being denied against them, by attributing them to Allah, and He defined the sons (al-banin) rather than the daughters, as an honouring of them over the daughters.

﴿And when one of them is given good news﴾: the explanation of its counterpart has already been given in Surat al-Nahl.

﴿Or one who is brought up in adornment﴾: i.e., he moves through his life state by state in ornament (al-hilyah), which is jewelry that is suitable only for females and not for males, because they adorn themselves with it for their husbands. And he, if he disputes, does not make clear, due to weakness of intellect and lack of reflection and contemplation; by this he showed their rights and the superiority of sons over them. In this there is an indication that it is not fitting for a man to adorn himself as a woman does, and that he should be rough. The stallion among men refuses to take on the attributes of women. The apparent meaning is that by "one who is brought up in adornment" He meant women. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: and this is indicated by His saying: ﴿while in dispute he is not clear﴾: i.e., he does not produce proof, nor establish evidence, nor reveal what is in his mind in a clear manner. It is said: you rarely find a woman who does not spoil speech and mix up meanings, to the extent that it was reported of some people that he said: "When we enter upon so-and-so, we do not leave until we know that her intellect is the intellect of a woman." Ibn Zayd said: what is meant by "one who is brought up in adornment" is idols, for they used to make many of them from gold and silver, and place jewelry on many of them. This view is weakened by His saying: ﴿while in dispute he is not clear﴾, unless by negating clarity is meant negating dispute, i.e., there is no dispute from them, for it is like His saying:
"Over a well-trodden path whose landmark does not guide one."
i.e., there is no landmark for it so that one might be guided by it. "Man" (man) is in the accusative position, i.e., and they made for Him those who are brought up. It is permissible that it be in the nominative position by way of the inchoative, i.e., whoever is brought up, they made for Allah. The majority read yunasha'u (is brought up) in the active voice; al-Jahdari in one report read it in the passive voice, lightened; Ibn 'Abbas, Zayd ibn 'Ali, al-Hasan, Mujahid, al-Jahdari in one narration, al-Akhawan (the two brothers), Hafs, al-Mufaddal, Aban, Ibn Miqsam and Harun, from Abu 'Amr: in the passive voice, intensified; and al-Hasan in one narration: yunasha'u on the pattern of yufa'alu, in the passive voice, and al-munasha'ah means the same as al-insha', like al-mu'alah means al-i'la'. "In disputation" (fi al-khisam) is connected to an omitted element whose explanation is "not clear," i.e., and he does not make clear in disputation. Whoever permits "amma zaydan ghayru daribin" by making the object of "ghayr" operate, permits that it be connected to "mubin," treating "ghayr" as "la." The placing of the complement of "amma" after "la" is a matter of disagreement, and this has been mentioned in grammar.

[p. 2]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat al-Zukhruf: eighty-nine verses, Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

[p. 3]

﴿Ha Mim.﴾ ﴿By the Book that makes things clear,﴾ ﴿indeed We have made it an Arabic Qur'an, that you may understand.﴾ ﴿And indeed it is, in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and wise.﴾ ﴿Shall We withhold the Reminder from you and turn away from you, because you are a people who transgress?﴾ ﴿How many a prophet did We send among the earlier peoples?﴾ ﴿Yet no prophet came to them but they mocked him.﴾ ﴿So We destroyed those who were stronger than these in might, and the example of the earlier peoples has passed on.﴾ ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "The Mighty, the All-Knowing created them."﴾ ﴿Who made the earth for you as a cradle and made for you therein roads, that you may be guided.﴾ ﴿And who sends down water from the sky in measure, and We revive with it a dead land. Thus you will be brought forth.﴾ ﴿And who created all the pairs and made for you ships and cattle on which you ride,﴾ ﴿that you may sit firmly upon their backs and then remember the favour of your Lord when you are settled upon them, and say, "Glory be to Him who has subjected these to us, and we could not have subdued them ourselves.﴾ ﴿And indeed to our Lord we will return."﴾ ﴿And they have attributed to Him a portion of His servants. Indeed, mankind is clearly ungrateful.﴾ ﴿Has He taken daughters from what He creates and chosen sons for you?﴾ ﴿And when one of them is given news of what he attributes to the Most Gracious, his face darkens, and he is suppressed with grief.﴾ ﴿Is one who is raised in ornament, and who in dispute is not clear?﴾ ﴿And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Gracious, into females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned.﴾ [43:19] ﴿And they say, "If the Most Gracious had willed, we would not have worshipped them." They have no knowledge of that; they only guess.﴾ [43:20] ﴿Did We give them a Book before this, so that they hold fast to it?﴾ [43:21] ﴿Rather, they say, "We found our fathers following a religion, and we are guided by their footsteps."﴾ [43:22] ﴿And thus We did not send a warner before you to any town except that its affluent people said, "We found our fathers following a religion, and we follow in their footsteps."﴾ [43:23] ﴿He said, "Even if I bring you better guidance than what you found your fathers following?" They said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with."﴾ [43:24] ﴿So We took retribution from them. Then see how was the end of the deniers.﴾ [43:25] ﴿And when Abraham said to his father and his people, "Indeed, I am free of what you worship,﴾ [43:26] ﴿except He who originated me, for He will guide me."﴾ [43:27] ﴿And he made it a lasting word among his descendants, that they might return.﴾ [43:28] ﴿Rather, I gave enjoyment to these people and their fathers until the truth and a clear messenger came to them.﴾ [43:29] ﴿And when the truth came to them they said, "This is magic, and we disbelieve in it."﴾ [43:30] ﴿And they said, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from the two cities?"﴾ [43:31] ﴿Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord? We have distributed among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others in rank, that some may take others in service. But the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate.﴾ [43:32] ﴿And were it not that people would become one community, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Gracious roofs of silver for their houses and staircases by which they ascend,﴾ [43:33] ﴿and doors for their houses and couches on which they recline,﴾ [43:34] ﴿and ornaments of gold. But all that is merely the enjoyment of the life of this world, while the Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous.﴾ [43:35] ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Gracious, We appoint for him a devil, and he is his companion.﴾ [43:36] ﴿And indeed they hinder them from the way, while they think they are guided.﴾ [43:37] ﴿Until, when he comes to Us, he says, "Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! What an evil companion!"﴾ [43:38] ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you did wrong, that you will be sharers in the punishment.﴾ [43:39] ﴿Can you, then, make the deaf hear, or guide the blind and those who are in clear error?﴾ [43:40] ﴿And whether We take you away, indeed We will take retribution from them,﴾ [43:41] ﴿or We show you that which We promised them, indeed We are Able over them.﴾ [43:42] ﴿So hold fast to what has been revealed to you. Indeed, you are upon a straight path.﴾ [43:43] ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people, and you will be questioned.﴾ [43:44] ﴿And ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Gracious?﴾ [43:45] ﴿And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, and he said, "Indeed, I am a messenger of the Lord of the worlds."﴾ [43:46] ﴿But when he brought them Our signs, at once they laughed at them.﴾ [43:47] ﴿And We did not show them a sign except that it was greater than its companion, and We seized them with punishment that they might return.﴾ [43:48] ﴿And they said, "O magician, invoke your Lord for us by what He has promised you. Indeed, we will be guided."﴾ [43:49] ﴿But when We removed the punishment from them, at once they broke their word.﴾ [43:50] ﴿And Pharaoh proclaimed among his people, saying, "O my people, is not the kingdom of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me? Do you not see?﴾ [43:51] ﴿Am I not better than this one who is contemptible and can hardly express himself?﴾ [43:52] ﴿Why then have bracelets of gold not been cast upon him, or angels not come with him in succession?"﴾ [43:53] ﴿So he made light of his people, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a defiant people.﴾ [43:54] ﴿And when they angered Us, We took retribution from them and drowned them all,﴾ [43:55] ﴿and We made them a precedent and an example for later generations.﴾ [43:56] ﴿And when the son of Mary was cited as an example, at once your people turned away from it.﴾ [43:57] ﴿And they said, "Are our gods better, or is he?" They cited him to you only for argument. Rather, they are a contentious people.﴾ [43:58] ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favour, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel.﴾ [43:59] ﴿And if We willed, We would have made from you angels to succeed one another on the earth.﴾ [43:60] ﴿And indeed, he is a sign of the Hour, so do not doubt it, and follow Me. This is a straight path.﴾ [43:61] ﴿And let not Satan hinder you; indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.﴾ [43:62] ﴿And when Jesus came with clear proofs, he said, "I have come to you with wisdom, and to make clear to you some of that about which you differ. So fear Allah and obey me.﴾ [43:63] ﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path."﴾ [43:64] ﴿Then the factions differed among themselves. So woe to those who did wrong, from the punishment of a painful Day.﴾ [43:65] ﴿Do they await only the Hour, that it should come upon them suddenly while they are unaware?﴾ [43:66] ﴿On that Day, intimate friends will be enemies to one another, except the righteous.﴾ [43:67] ﴿"O My servants, no fear will be upon you today, nor will you grieve,﴾ [43:68] ﴿those who believed in Our signs and were Muslims."﴾ [43:69] ﴿"Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, rejoicing."﴾ [43:70] ﴿There will be circulated among them platters of gold and cups, and therein is whatever the souls desire and eyes delight in, and you will abide therein eternally.﴾ [43:71] ﴿And that is the Paradise which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do.﴾ [43:72] ﴿For you therein is abundant fruit, from which you will eat.﴾ [43:73] ﴿Indeed, the criminals will abide eternally in the punishment of Hell.﴾ [43:74] ﴿It will not be lightened for them, and they will be therein in despair.﴾ [43:75] ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they were the wrongdoers.﴾ [43:76] ﴿And they will call, "O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us." He will say, "Indeed, you will remain."﴾ [43:77] ﴿Certainly We brought you the truth, but most of you are averse to the truth.﴾ [43:78] ﴿Or have they devised a plan? Indeed, We too are devising.﴾ [43:79] ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private talk? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, writing.﴾ [43:80] ﴿Say, "If the Most Gracious had a son, I would be the first of the worshippers."﴾ [43:81] ﴿Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.﴾ [43:82] ﴿So leave them to wade in falsehood and play until they meet their Day which they are promised.﴾ [43:83] ﴿And He is the One who is God in the heaven and God on the earth, and He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing.﴾ [43:84] ﴿Blessed is He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and with Him is the knowledge of the Hour, and to Him you will be returned.﴾ [43:85] ﴿And those whom they invoke besides Him possess no intercession, except one who testifies to the truth and they know.﴾ [43:86] ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah." Then how are they deluded?﴾ [43:87] ﴿And [Muhammad's] saying, "O my Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe."﴾ [43:88] ﴿So overlook them and say, "Peace." But they will come to know.﴾ [43:89]

(p. 4)

(Ya'shu): yu'ridu (turns away), and ya'sha: ya'ma (becomes blind). Ibn Qutaybah said: "I have not seen anyone report 'ashawtu 'an al-shay'' meaning 'I turned away from it.' Rather it is said: ta'ashaytu 'an kadha and ta'amaytu, when one pretends not to notice it. And one says: 'ashawtu ila al-nar, when one seeks guidance toward it with weak sight." It is also said: 'ashan ya'sha, when an affliction occurs in his sight. And 'asha ya'shu: he looked, being blind, without any affliction in him, as one says: 'araja (limps) for one who has a limp, and 'araja for one who walks with the gait of a lame man without a limp. Al-Hutay'ah said:

"Whenever you come to him, you squint toward the light of his fire; you will find there the best fire and the best hearth."

That is: you look at it with the gaze of one whose sight is weakened by the great blaze of the fire there. From this is the saying of Hatim:

"I squint when my neighbour appears, until the curtain screens my neighbour."

(al-Suhfah): al-Jawhari said: it is the bowl. Al-Kisa'i said: the largest of bowls is the jafnah, then the qas'ah which holds ten, then the suhfah which holds five, then the makilah which holds two or three men. And al-sahifah (the book) pl. suhuf and saha'if.

(al-Kub): Qutrub said: it is the ewer that has no handle. Al-Akhfash said: the ewer has no spout. It is said: it is like the ewer, except it has no ear or grip. Abu Mansur al-Jawaliqi said: it was without a handle so that the drinker may drink from wherever he wishes, because the handle turns the drinker away from some directions. End of quotation. 'Adi said:

"Reclining, its doors clap; a servant runs around him with the cup."

(Abram): al-Farra' said: abram al-amr means he strove to make it firm; and abram al-qatil means when he doubled the killing, which is the second killing, and the first is called sijjil, as Zuhayr said:

"Of sijjil and barm."

End of quotation. Al-ibram is to join two threads and twist them with firm twisting, and al-barim is a thread that has two colours.

* *

(p. 5)

Ha Mim. By the Book that makes things clear… [the verses 43:1–19 are repeated here as in the opening, ending at ﴿أوَمَن يُنَشَّأُ في الحِلْيَةِ وهو في الخِصامِ غَيْرُ مُبِينٍ﴾ (43:18)]

This surah is Meccan. Muqatil said: except His saying, ﴿Ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers﴾ (43:45). Ibn 'Atiyyah said: by the consensus of the people of knowledge.

﴿Indeed, We have made it﴾: that is, We have made it into, or named it. It is the answer to the oath, and it is one of the fine kinds of oath because of the correspondence between the oath and what is sworn to, and because both are of one kind. A similar example is the saying of Abu Tammam:

"Your front teeth, indeed they are ighrid (fresh and tender)."

Some say: "the Book" (al-Kitab) here refers to the revealed scriptures, and the pronoun in "We made it" (ja'alnahu) refers to the Qur'an, even though it has not been explicitly mentioned before, because the meaning points to it. Al-Zamakhshari said: "ja'alnahu" means "We rendered it" (sayyarnahu), transitive to two objects, or it means "We created it" (khalaqnahu), transitive to one object, like His words: ﴿And He made the darknesses and the light﴾ [al-An'am: 1]. "(An Arabic Qur'an)" is a circumstantial accusative (hal). "La'alla" is used figuratively to mean intention (irada), so as to take into account both its meaning and the meaning of hope (tarajji), i.e., "We created it Arabic, not foreign." He intended that the Arabs might understand it, and lest they say: ﴿Why are its verses not made distinct?﴾ [Fussilat: 44]. End of quote. This is in line with the Mu'tazili position that the Qur'an is created. "The Mother of the Book" (umm al-kitab) is the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), because it is the origin in which the books were recorded. This contains an honouring of the Qur'an and an elevation of it, in that it is with Him "exalted" above all the books and "lofty" above all forms of corruption. "Wise" (hakim) means ruling over all the other books, or "made firm" (muhkam), being in the utmost eloquence, fluency and soundness of meanings. Qatadah, Ikrimah and al-Suddi said: the Preserved Tablet is the Qur'an, in which all of it is abrogated (mansukh), and from it Jibril used to descend. It is also said: "the Mother of the Book" refers to the clear verses (al-muhkamat), according to His words: ﴿He it is who has sent down to you the Book; in it are clear verses, they are the mother of the Book﴾ [Al 'Imran: 7]. Its meaning is that the sura of Ha-Mim is among the clear verses which are the mother. Al-Jumhur read "fi umm" with a dammah on the hamzah, while al-Akhawan read it with a kasrah; Yusuf ibn 'Amr attributed it to Iraq, and Ibn 'Atiyyah did not attribute it to al-Akhawan, out of oversight on his part. It is said: "darab 'an kadha" and "a'rada 'anhu", when he turned away from it. "And the Reminder" (al-dhikr): al-Dahhak and Abu Salih said it means the Qur'an, i.e., "Shall We turn away from you the Reminder?" The saying of the Arabs: "darab al-gharaib 'an al-hawd", when he drove them away and pushed them off. The poet said:
"Strike off from you the cares that come upon you, a blow like the sword's blow on the forelock of the horse."
It is also said: "the Reminder" means the call to God and warning of His punishment. Al-Zamakhshari said: The "fa" is for coordination with an omitted element, its estimate being: "Shall We neglect you, so that We strike away the Reminder from you," in denial that the matter should be contrary to what was previously stated of Our sending down the Book and making it an Arabic Qur'an so that you may understand it and act upon its requirements. End of quote. The discussion of his estimating a verb between the hamzah and the fa was previously given, as in: "Have they not travelled?" (afalam yasiru) and "Will you not understand?" (afala ta'qilun), and between it and the waw, as in "Have they not travelled?" (awalam yasiru). The correct position is the view of Sibawayh and the grammarians that the fa and the waw are intended to be placed first, to coordinate what follows them with what precedes them, and that the hamzah came first because interrogation has the front position in speech. There is no disagreement between the hamzah and the particle, and we have already answered his statement. Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said the meaning is: "Shall We abandon your admonition and your warning, pardoning you and pardoning your sins, if you were, or because you were, a people who exceed the limits?" That is, this is not appropriate. Qatadah inclined to the view that the meaning is "safhan", i.e., forgiven, i.e., we leave it; then you will not be held to account for its words or its arrangement, nor will you be alerted to it. This meaning is like the verse of the poet:
"The breeze passes by the dweller of Dhi al-Fada with forgiveness, and it splits my heart that its blowing should come."
And like the saying of Kuthayyir:
"Forgiving, so you meet her only as a miserly one, and whoever tires of that union, she too tires of it."
Ibn 'Abbas said: the meaning is: "Do you suppose that We will overlook you, while you have not done what you were commanded?" Al-Kalbi said: "that We leave you neglected, without command or prohibition?" Mujahid also said: "that We will not punish you for denying?" It is said: "that We abandon the sending down of the Qur'an because of your denial?" Hassan ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Dab'i, al-Sumayt ibn 'Umayr and Shumayl ibn 'Udhrah read "suhfan" with a dammah on the sad, while al-Jumhur read it with a fathah; both are dialects, like "al-sadd" and "al-sudd". The accusative of "safhan" is as a verbal noun (masdar) from the meaning of "afa-nadribu", because its meaning is "afa-nasfahu"; or it is a verbal noun in the position of a circumstantial, i.e., "turning away," as al-Hawfi said, and Abu al-Baqa' followed him. Al-Zamakhshari said: "safhan" has two aspects: either it is a verbal noun from "safaha 'anhu", when he turned away, put in the accusative as an object for a purpose, in the sense: "Shall We withdraw from you the sending down of the Qur'an and the imposition of the proof by it, turning away from you?"; or in the sense of the side, from their saying: "he looked at him with the side of his face," and the side of his face, in the sense of: "Shall We set it aside from you as a side?" so it is put in the accusative as an adverb of place, as you say: "put it aside," and "walk aside." The reading of whoever read "suf-han" with a dammah supports this. In this reading there is another aspect, which is that it be a lightened form of "suhuf", the plural of "sahif", and be in the accusative as a circumstantial, i.e., turning away and averting. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "safhan", its accusative is like the accusative of "sun'a Allah" (the work of God). End of quote. He means that it is a verbal noun emphasising the content of the preceding sentence, so the governing element is omitted; but what he said does not appear to be the case, for its accusative is not like the accusative of "sun'a Allah." Nafi' and al-Akhawan read "in" with a kasrah on the hamzah, yet their transgressing was certain. How, then, does the conditional "in" enter upon it, which only enters upon what is not certain, or upon what is certain but whose time is indefinite? Al-Zamakhshari said: It is of the type of condition that I mentioned as issuing from one who is confident in the correctness of the matter, certain of its establishment, as a hired worker says: "If I have worked for you, then pay me my due," while he knows that, but he gives the impression in his speech that your neglect in departing from the right is the act of one who has doubt about the entitlement, despite its clarity, to make him appear ignorant. Al-Jumhur read "an" with a fathah on the hamzah, meaning: "because you were." The poet said:
"Do you lament that the departing companion has gone?"
Zayd ibn 'Ali read "idh kuntum" with a dhal in place of the nun, when He mentioned an address to the Quraysh: "Shall We turn away from you the Reminder?" This denial was evidence of their denial of the Messenger and a denial of what he had brought. God comforted him by informing him that their habit was the habit of the earlier nations, mocking the messengers, and that God destroyed those who were more mighty in strength than Quraysh, that is, greater in number, in equipment and in stamina.
"And the example of the former peoples has passed": that is, let Quraysh beware lest there befall them the like of what befell the former peoples who denied the messengers, of punishment. This was said by Qatadah: it is the punishment which travelled as a proverb. It is also said: the example of the former peoples in disbelief and denial, and Quraysh had taken their path; the address to them in His words "Shall We turn away from you" had been directed, then He turned from them to report in the third person in His words: "So We destroyed those who were more mighty than them in strength." (And if you ask them): this is an argument against Quraysh with what necessitates contradiction, namely their acknowledgement that the creator of the upper and lower worlds is God, yet they take idols as gods besides God, worshipping and magnifying them. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: the requirement of the answer is that they should say "God created them," but when God mentioned the meaning, the expression about God came as "the Mighty, the Knowing", so that this would be a preparation for the attributes He enumerated, whose announcement He began and which He detached from the speech whose meaning He related from Quraysh. End of quote. Al-Zamakhshari said: they would attribute the creation of them to the One whose attributes these are, and they would ascribe it to Him. End of quote. The apparent meaning is that "the Mighty, the Knowing created them" is the very speech reported from them, and the fact that they mention "God created them" in one place does not prevent them from saying in another question: "The Mighty, the Knowing created them."

"Who made for you": is part of God's speech, addressed to them, reminding them of His previous blessings. He repeated the verb in the answer in His words: "the Mighty, the Knowing created them," for emphasis. In places other than a question, they confined themselves to mentioning the name of God, since He is the proper name comprising the lofty attributes, and the answer corresponds to the question in meaning, not in wording, because "man" is a subject. If it corresponded in wording, it would be with the noun as subject, not with the verb. "So that you may be guided": that is, to your destinations in travel, or that you may be guided by reflection and consideration. "In measure": that is, by decree and determination from eternity, or by sufficiency, not so much that it corrupts, nor so little that it does not avail.

"Then We revived": that is, We gave life by it.
"A dead land": it is mentioned in terms of the rain, and "land" (baldah) is a collective noun. Abu Ja'far and 'Isa read "mayyitan" with a shaddah. Al-Jumhur read "tukhrajun" as passive, while Ibn Wathhab, 'Abd Allah ibn Jubayr al-Mus'bih, 'Isa, Ibn 'Amir and al-Akhawan read it as active. "Al-azwaj": the kinds of everything. It is said: everything other than God is a pair (zawj), like above and below, right and left, front and back, past and future, essences and attributes, summer and winter, spring and autumn. That they are pairs indicates that they are possible in existence, and it indicates that their Originator is single, namely God, exalted above opposites, counterparts and rivals. End of quote.

"And the cattle": the known thing is that only camels are ridden among the cattle. "Ma" is a relative pronoun, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e., what they ride. "Rakiba" is used in relation to causes, and it takes the object directly, while it takes it through "fi" in the sense of the implied "ma yarkabunahu." The lam in "li-tastawu" (so that you may sit firmly): the apparent reading is that it is the lam of purpose. Al-Hawfi said: whoever affirms the lam of becoming may also say so here. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: it is the lam of command, but there is a distance here because of using the imperative of the addressee with the ta of address, which is so rare that it should not be analogised. The eloquent and common form is "idrib," and it is said "li-tadrib"; indeed the grammarians stated that it is a bad and rare dialect, hardly known except as an irregular reading. Therefore, with it, "fal-tafrahu" is read with the ta for address. What the traditionists transmitted from his words, peace be upon him, "li-ta'khudhu masaffakum" (take your ranks), though there is a possibility that the narrator related it by meaning, and the saying of the poet:
"Let you stand, O son of the best of Quraysh, so that you may fulfil the needs of the Muslims."
Al-Zajjaj claimed that it is a good dialect, but this contradicts what the grammarians claimed. The pronoun in "zuhurihi" returns to "ma", as if he said: "on the backs of what you ride," as Abu 'Ubaydah said; hence the plural was appropriate, because its consequence is both word and meaning. Whoever uses the plural does so with regard to meaning, and whoever uses the singular with regard to wording; and what is meant is "of the ships and the cattle." Al-Farra' said something similar, saying: he attributed the backs to them. "Then you may remember" (thumma tadhkaru): that is, in your hearts, "the blessing of your Lord," acknowledging it and magnifying it. He does not mean remembrance by the tongue but by the heart; for this reason He set against it His words: "and say: Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us." That is, glorify God by explicit speech. It has come in a hadith that when he, peace be upon him, put his foot in the stirrup he would say: "In the name of God," and when he settled upon the mount he would say: "Praise be to God for every state; glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and to Him we are returning," and he would say "Allahu akbar" three times and "La ilaha illa Allah" three times. They also said: when one boards a ship he says: "In the name of God is its course and its anchorage" up to "Merciful," and at disembarking one says: "O God, cause us to alight at a blessed landing place, for You are the best of those who cause to alight."

"Qarn" (ability): the one who is dominant, controlling, capable of a thing; it is said: "aqrana al-shay'," when he was able to manage it. Ibn Hermah said:
"You have made able what you laid upon me, and little is it that endurance bears the rejection and the forsaking, O Da'd."
The literal sense of "aqranahu" is that he found it a counterpart to himself, and that which is bound to it. For the difficult does not become a counterpart to the weak. The poet said:
"And the son of the camel-colt, when he is tied with a rope, cannot withstand the charge of the stout, long-necked camels."
"Qarn" is also the rope with which something is tied. Abu 'Ubayd said: "Fulan muqrin li-fulan," meaning he controls him. The meaning is that we have no strength to control the beast and the ship; it is God who subjected them. Qutrub recited for 'Amr ibn Ma'dikarib:
"Indeed the tribes know that 'Aqil, in our favour in the calamities, is not one who subdues us."
It was also read "lamuqtarinin," the active participle of "iqtarana."

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 43, verse 1–18 (part 3 of 3):

﴿And indeed, to our Lord we are returning﴾: i.e., returning (raji'un). This is an affirmation of the return to Allah and of the Resurrection (al-ba'th), because the rider is in a position of possible destruction by drowning when he boards a ship, and by being thrown from a mount, since riding an animal is a matter fraught with danger, and safety in it is not assured. So his saying this is a reminder that he is conscious of the eventual return to Allah and prepared to meet Him, and he does not leave that from his heart or his tongue.

﴿And they have made for Him﴾: i.e., the disbelievers of Quraysh and the Arabs have made for Him, i.e., for Allah, (min 'ibadihi) of His servants: i.e., from among those who are the servants of Allah, (juz'an), a portion. Mujahid said: a share and a lot, and this is the saying of the Arabs: "The angels are the daughters of Allah." Qatadah said: juz'an, i.e., a rival (nid), and that is the idols, Pharaoh, and whoever was worshipped besides Allah. It was also said: al-juz' means females. Some of the linguists said: it is said "ajza'at al-mar'ah" when she gives birth to a female. The poet said:
"If a free woman bears a female one day, there is no wonder, for a free woman sometimes bears a male."
It was said: this verse is fabricated, and likewise his saying:
"He married her to one of the daughters of al-Aws, one who bears females."

Since it had been mentioned that they acknowledge that He, the Exalted, is the Creator of the world, He rebuked them for making for Him a part, while they have acknowledged that He is the Creator. How then do they describe Him with an attribute of the created? ﴿Indeed, man is clearly ungrateful﴾ for the blessing of his Creator. (mubin): manifest in his denial. What is meant by "man" is the one who makes for Allah a part, and others among the disbelievers. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "mubin" in this place is intransitive. End of quote. It is not necessarily restricted to what he mentioned; rather, its meaning may be that it is apparent in ingratitude for blessings and manifest in his denial, as we have said.

﴿Has He taken daughters from what He creates?﴾: an interrogative of denial and rebuke for the scantiness of their intellects. How did they claim that He, the Exalted, took for Himself what you yourselves hate, when you yourselves, when news of them is brought to you, your faces darken, and you bury them alive? (wa-asfakum): He made for you the choicest of what is beloved, and that is sons. His saying (min ma yakhluqu) is an alert to the impossibility of offspring, whether male or female; and even if the taking of offspring is supposed, how would He choose for Himself the lesser and reserve the higher for you? He mentioned the daughters first because they are the ones being denied against them, by attributing them to Allah, and He defined the sons (al-banin) rather than the daughters, as an honouring of them over the daughters.

﴿And when one of them is given good news﴾: the explanation of its counterpart has already been given in Surat al-Nahl.

﴿Or one who is brought up in adornment﴾: i.e., he moves through his life state by state in ornament (al-hilyah), which is jewelry that is suitable only for females and not for males, because they adorn themselves with it for their husbands. And he, if he disputes, does not make clear, due to weakness of intellect and lack of reflection and contemplation; by this he showed their rights and the superiority of sons over them. In this there is an indication that it is not fitting for a man to adorn himself as a woman does, and that he should be rough. The stallion among men refuses to take on the attributes of women. The apparent meaning is that by "one who is brought up in adornment" He meant women. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: and this is indicated by His saying: ﴿while in dispute he is not clear﴾: i.e., he does not produce proof, nor establish evidence, nor reveal what is in his mind in a clear manner. It is said: you rarely find a woman who does not spoil speech and mix up meanings, to the extent that it was reported of some people that he said: "When we enter upon so-and-so, we do not leave until we know that her intellect is the intellect of a woman." Ibn Zayd said: what is meant by "one who is brought up in adornment" is idols, for they used to make many of them from gold and silver, and place jewelry on many of them. This view is weakened by His saying: ﴿while in dispute he is not clear﴾, unless by negating clarity is meant negating dispute, i.e., there is no dispute from them, for it is like His saying:
"Over a well-trodden path whose landmark does not guide one."
i.e., there is no landmark for it so that one might be guided by it. "Man" (man) is in the accusative position, i.e., and they made for Him those who are brought up. It is permissible that it be in the nominative position by way of the inchoative, i.e., whoever is brought up, they made for Allah. The majority read yunasha'u (is brought up) in the active voice; al-Jahdari in one report read it in the passive voice, lightened; Ibn 'Abbas, Zayd ibn 'Ali, al-Hasan, Mujahid, al-Jahdari in one narration, al-Akhawan (the two brothers), Hafs, al-Mufaddal, Aban, Ibn Miqsam and Harun, from Abu 'Amr: in the passive voice, intensified; and al-Hasan in one narration: yunasha'u on the pattern of yufa'alu, in the passive voice, and al-munasha'ah means the same as al-insha', like al-mu'alah means al-i'la'. "In disputation" (fi al-khisam) is connected to an omitted element whose explanation is "not clear," i.e., and he does not make clear in disputation. Whoever permits "amma zaydan ghayru daribin" by making the object of "ghayr" operate, permits that it be connected to "mubin," treating "ghayr" as "la." The placing of the complement of "amma" after "la" is a matter of disagreement, and this has been mentioned in grammar.

[p. 2]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat al-Zukhruf: eighty-nine verses, Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

[p. 3]

﴿Ha Mim.﴾ ﴿By the Book that makes things clear,﴾ ﴿indeed We have made it an Arabic Qur'an, that you may understand.﴾ ﴿And indeed it is, in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and wise.﴾ ﴿Shall We withhold the Reminder from you and turn away from you, because you are a people who transgress?﴾ ﴿How many a prophet did We send among the earlier peoples?﴾ ﴿Yet no prophet came to them but they mocked him.﴾ ﴿So We destroyed those who were stronger than these in might, and the example of the earlier peoples has passed on.﴾ ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "The Mighty, the All-Knowing created them."﴾ ﴿Who made the earth for you as a cradle and made for you therein roads, that you may be guided.﴾ ﴿And who sends down water from the sky in measure, and We revive with it a dead land. Thus you will be brought forth.﴾ ﴿And who created all the pairs and made for you ships and cattle on which you ride,﴾ ﴿that you may sit firmly upon their backs and then remember the favour of your Lord when you are settled upon them, and say, "Glory be to Him who has subjected these to us, and we could not have subdued them ourselves.﴾ ﴿And indeed to our Lord we will return."﴾ ﴿And they have attributed to Him a portion of His servants. Indeed, mankind is clearly ungrateful.﴾ ﴿Has He taken daughters from what He creates and chosen sons for you?﴾ ﴿And when one of them is given news of what he attributes to the Most Gracious, his face darkens, and he is suppressed with grief.﴾ ﴿Is one who is raised in ornament, and who in dispute is not clear?﴾ ﴿And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Gracious, into females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned.﴾ [43:19] ﴿And they say, "If the Most Gracious had willed, we would not have worshipped them." They have no knowledge of that; they only guess.﴾ [43:20] ﴿Did We give them a Book before this, so that they hold fast to it?﴾ [43:21] ﴿Rather, they say, "We found our fathers following a religion, and we are guided by their footsteps."﴾ [43:22] ﴿And thus We did not send a warner before you to any town except that its affluent people said, "We found our fathers following a religion, and we follow in their footsteps."﴾ [43:23] ﴿He said, "Even if I bring you better guidance than what you found your fathers following?" They said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with."﴾ [43:24] ﴿So We took retribution from them. Then see how was the end of the deniers.﴾ [43:25] ﴿And when Abraham said to his father and his people, "Indeed, I am free of what you worship,﴾ [43:26] ﴿except He who originated me, for He will guide me."﴾ [43:27] ﴿And he made it a lasting word among his descendants, that they might return.﴾ [43:28] ﴿Rather, I gave enjoyment to these people and their fathers until the truth and a clear messenger came to them.﴾ [43:29] ﴿And when the truth came to them they said, "This is magic, and we disbelieve in it."﴾ [43:30] ﴿And they said, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from the two cities?"﴾ [43:31] ﴿Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord? We have distributed among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others in rank, that some may take others in service. But the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate.﴾ [43:32] ﴿And were it not that people would become one community, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Gracious roofs of silver for their houses and staircases by which they ascend,﴾ [43:33] ﴿and doors for their houses and couches on which they recline,﴾ [43:34] ﴿and ornaments of gold. But all that is merely the enjoyment of the life of this world, while the Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous.﴾ [43:35] ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Gracious, We appoint for him a devil, and he is his companion.﴾ [43:36] ﴿And indeed they hinder them from the way, while they think they are guided.﴾ [43:37] ﴿Until, when he comes to Us, he says, "Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! What an evil companion!"﴾ [43:38] ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you did wrong, that you will be sharers in the punishment.﴾ [43:39] ﴿Can you, then, make the deaf hear, or guide the blind and those who are in clear error?﴾ [43:40] ﴿And whether We take you away, indeed We will take retribution from them,﴾ [43:41] ﴿or We show you that which We promised them, indeed We are Able over them.﴾ [43:42] ﴿So hold fast to what has been revealed to you. Indeed, you are upon a straight path.﴾ [43:43] ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people, and you will be questioned.﴾ [43:44] ﴿And ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Gracious?﴾ [43:45] ﴿And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, and he said, "Indeed, I am a messenger of the Lord of the worlds."﴾ [43:46] ﴿But when he brought them Our signs, at once they laughed at them.﴾ [43:47] ﴿And We did not show them a sign except that it was greater than its companion, and We seized them with punishment that they might return.﴾ [43:48] ﴿And they said, "O magician, invoke your Lord for us by what He has promised you. Indeed, we will be guided."﴾ [43:49] ﴿But when We removed the punishment from them, at once they broke their word.﴾ [43:50] ﴿And Pharaoh proclaimed among his people, saying, "O my people, is not the kingdom of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me? Do you not see?﴾ [43:51] ﴿Am I not better than this one who is contemptible and can hardly express himself?﴾ [43:52] ﴿Why then have bracelets of gold not been cast upon him, or angels not come with him in succession?"﴾ [43:53] ﴿So he made light of his people, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a defiant people.﴾ [43:54] ﴿And when they angered Us, We took retribution from them and drowned them all,﴾ [43:55] ﴿and We made them a precedent and an example for later generations.﴾ [43:56] ﴿And when the son of Mary was cited as an example, at once your people turned away from it.﴾ [43:57] ﴿And they said, "Are our gods better, or is he?" They cited him to you only for argument. Rather, they are a contentious people.﴾ [43:58] ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favour, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel.﴾ [43:59] ﴿And if We willed, We would have made from you angels to succeed one another on the earth.﴾ [43:60] ﴿And indeed, he is a sign of the Hour, so do not doubt it, and follow Me. This is a straight path.﴾ [43:61] ﴿And let not Satan hinder you; indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.﴾ [43:62] ﴿And when Jesus came with clear proofs, he said, "I have come to you with wisdom, and to make clear to you some of that about which you differ. So fear Allah and obey me.﴾ [43:63] ﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path."﴾ [43:64] ﴿Then the factions differed among themselves. So woe to those who did wrong, from the punishment of a painful Day.﴾ [43:65] ﴿Do they await only the Hour, that it should come upon them suddenly while they are unaware?﴾ [43:66] ﴿On that Day, intimate friends will be enemies to one another, except the righteous.﴾ [43:67] ﴿"O My servants, no fear will be upon you today, nor will you grieve,﴾ [43:68] ﴿those who believed in Our signs and were Muslims."﴾ [43:69] ﴿"Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, rejoicing."﴾ [43:70] ﴿There will be circulated among them platters of gold and cups, and therein is whatever the souls desire and eyes delight in, and you will abide therein eternally.﴾ [43:71] ﴿And that is the Paradise which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do.﴾ [43:72] ﴿For you therein is abundant fruit, from which you will eat.﴾ [43:73] ﴿Indeed, the criminals will abide eternally in the punishment of Hell.﴾ [43:74] ﴿It will not be lightened for them, and they will be therein in despair.﴾ [43:75] ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they were the wrongdoers.﴾ [43:76] ﴿And they will call, "O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us." He will say, "Indeed, you will remain."﴾ [43:77] ﴿Certainly We brought you the truth, but most of you are averse to the truth.﴾ [43:78] ﴿Or have they devised a plan? Indeed, We too are devising.﴾ [43:79] ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private talk? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, writing.﴾ [43:80] ﴿Say, "If the Most Gracious had a son, I would be the first of the worshippers."﴾ [43:81] ﴿Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.﴾ [43:82] ﴿So leave them to wade in falsehood and play until they meet their Day which they are promised.﴾ [43:83] ﴿And He is the One who is God in the heaven and God on the earth, and He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing.﴾ [43:84] ﴿Blessed is He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and with Him is the knowledge of the Hour, and to Him you will be returned.﴾ [43:85] ﴿And those whom they invoke besides Him possess no intercession, except one who testifies to the truth and they know.﴾ [43:86] ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah." Then how are they deluded?﴾ [43:87] ﴿And [Muhammad's] saying, "O my Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe."﴾ [43:88] ﴿So overlook them and say, "Peace." But they will come to know.﴾ [43:89]

(p. 4)

(Ya'shu): yu'ridu (turns away), and ya'sha: ya'ma (becomes blind). Ibn Qutaybah said: "I have not seen anyone report 'ashawtu 'an al-shay'' meaning 'I turned away from it.' Rather it is said: ta'ashaytu 'an kadha and ta'amaytu, when one pretends not to notice it. And one says: 'ashawtu ila al-nar, when one seeks guidance toward it with weak sight." It is also said: 'ashan ya'sha, when an affliction occurs in his sight. And 'asha ya'shu: he looked, being blind, without any affliction in him, as one says: 'araja (limps) for one who has a limp, and 'araja for one who walks with the gait of a lame man without a limp. Al-Hutay'ah said:

"Whenever you come to him, you squint toward the light of his fire; you will find there the best fire and the best hearth."

That is: you look at it with the gaze of one whose sight is weakened by the great blaze of the fire there. From this is the saying of Hatim:

"I squint when my neighbour appears, until the curtain screens my neighbour."

(al-Suhfah): al-Jawhari said: it is the bowl. Al-Kisa'i said: the largest of bowls is the jafnah, then the qas'ah which holds ten, then the suhfah which holds five, then the makilah which holds two or three men. And al-sahifah (the book) pl. suhuf and saha'if.

(al-Kub): Qutrub said: it is the ewer that has no handle. Al-Akhfash said: the ewer has no spout. It is said: it is like the ewer, except it has no ear or grip. Abu Mansur al-Jawaliqi said: it was without a handle so that the drinker may drink from wherever he wishes, because the handle turns the drinker away from some directions. End of quotation. 'Adi said:

"Reclining, its doors clap; a servant runs around him with the cup."

(Abram): al-Farra' said: abram al-amr means he strove to make it firm; and abram al-qatil means when he doubled the killing, which is the second killing, and the first is called sijjil, as Zuhayr said:

"Of sijjil and barm."

End of quotation. Al-ibram is to join two threads and twist them with firm twisting, and al-barim is a thread that has two colours.

* *

(p. 5)

Ha Mim. By the Book that makes things clear… [the verses 43:1–19 are repeated here as in the opening, ending at ﴿أوَمَن يُنَشَّأُ في الحِلْيَةِ وهو في الخِصامِ غَيْرُ مُبِينٍ﴾ (43:18)]

This surah is Meccan. Muqatil said: except His saying, ﴿Ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers﴾ (43:45). Ibn 'Atiyyah said: by the consensus of the people of knowledge.

﴿Indeed, We have made it﴾: that is, We have made it into, or named it. It is the answer to the oath, and it is one of the fine kinds of oath because of the correspondence between the oath and what is sworn to, and because both are of one kind. A similar example is the saying of Abu Tammam:

"Your front teeth, indeed they are ighrid (fresh and tender)."

Some say: "the Book" (al-Kitab) here refers to the revealed scriptures, and the pronoun in "We made it" (ja'alnahu) refers to the Qur'an, even though it has not been explicitly mentioned before, because the meaning points to it. Al-Zamakhshari said: "ja'alnahu" means "We rendered it" (sayyarnahu), transitive to two objects, or it means "We created it" (khalaqnahu), transitive to one object, like His words: ﴿And He made the darknesses and the light﴾ [al-An'am: 1]. "(An Arabic Qur'an)" is a circumstantial accusative (hal). "La'alla" is used figuratively to mean intention (irada), so as to take into account both its meaning and the meaning of hope (tarajji), i.e., "We created it Arabic, not foreign." He intended that the Arabs might understand it, and lest they say: ﴿Why are its verses not made distinct?﴾ [Fussilat: 44]. End of quote. This is in line with the Mu'tazili position that the Qur'an is created. "The Mother of the Book" (umm al-kitab) is the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), because it is the origin in which the books were recorded. This contains an honouring of the Qur'an and an elevation of it, in that it is with Him "exalted" above all the books and "lofty" above all forms of corruption. "Wise" (hakim) means ruling over all the other books, or "made firm" (muhkam), being in the utmost eloquence, fluency and soundness of meanings. Qatadah, Ikrimah and al-Suddi said: the Preserved Tablet is the Qur'an, in which all of it is abrogated (mansukh), and from it Jibril used to descend. It is also said: "the Mother of the Book" refers to the clear verses (al-muhkamat), according to His words: ﴿He it is who has sent down to you the Book; in it are clear verses, they are the mother of the Book﴾ [Al 'Imran: 7]. Its meaning is that the sura of Ha-Mim is among the clear verses which are the mother. Al-Jumhur read "fi umm" with a dammah on the hamzah, while al-Akhawan read it with a kasrah; Yusuf ibn 'Amr attributed it to Iraq, and Ibn 'Atiyyah did not attribute it to al-Akhawan, out of oversight on his part. It is said: "darab 'an kadha" and "a'rada 'anhu", when he turned away from it. "And the Reminder" (al-dhikr): al-Dahhak and Abu Salih said it means the Qur'an, i.e., "Shall We turn away from you the Reminder?" The saying of the Arabs: "darab al-gharaib 'an al-hawd", when he drove them away and pushed them off. The poet said:
"Strike off from you the cares that come upon you, a blow like the sword's blow on the forelock of the horse."
It is also said: "the Reminder" means the call to God and warning of His punishment. Al-Zamakhshari said: The "fa" is for coordination with an omitted element, its estimate being: "Shall We neglect you, so that We strike away the Reminder from you," in denial that the matter should be contrary to what was previously stated of Our sending down the Book and making it an Arabic Qur'an so that you may understand it and act upon its requirements. End of quote. The discussion of his estimating a verb between the hamzah and the fa was previously given, as in: "Have they not travelled?" (afalam yasiru) and "Will you not understand?" (afala ta'qilun), and between it and the waw, as in "Have they not travelled?" (awalam yasiru). The correct position is the view of Sibawayh and the grammarians that the fa and the waw are intended to be placed first, to coordinate what follows them with what precedes them, and that the hamzah came first because interrogation has the front position in speech. There is no disagreement between the hamzah and the particle, and we have already answered his statement. Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said the meaning is: "Shall We abandon your admonition and your warning, pardoning you and pardoning your sins, if you were, or because you were, a people who exceed the limits?" That is, this is not appropriate. Qatadah inclined to the view that the meaning is "safhan", i.e., forgiven, i.e., we leave it; then you will not be held to account for its words or its arrangement, nor will you be alerted to it. This meaning is like the verse of the poet:
"The breeze passes by the dweller of Dhi al-Fada with forgiveness, and it splits my heart that its blowing should come."
And like the saying of Kuthayyir:
"Forgiving, so you meet her only as a miserly one, and whoever tires of that union, she too tires of it."
Ibn 'Abbas said: the meaning is: "Do you suppose that We will overlook you, while you have not done what you were commanded?" Al-Kalbi said: "that We leave you neglected, without command or prohibition?" Mujahid also said: "that We will not punish you for denying?" It is said: "that We abandon the sending down of the Qur'an because of your denial?" Hassan ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Dab'i, al-Sumayt ibn 'Umayr and Shumayl ibn 'Udhrah read "suhfan" with a dammah on the sad, while al-Jumhur read it with a fathah; both are dialects, like "al-sadd" and "al-sudd". The accusative of "safhan" is as a verbal noun (masdar) from the meaning of "afa-nadribu", because its meaning is "afa-nasfahu"; or it is a verbal noun in the position of a circumstantial, i.e., "turning away," as al-Hawfi said, and Abu al-Baqa' followed him. Al-Zamakhshari said: "safhan" has two aspects: either it is a verbal noun from "safaha 'anhu", when he turned away, put in the accusative as an object for a purpose, in the sense: "Shall We withdraw from you the sending down of the Qur'an and the imposition of the proof by it, turning away from you?"; or in the sense of the side, from their saying: "he looked at him with the side of his face," and the side of his face, in the sense of: "Shall We set it aside from you as a side?" so it is put in the accusative as an adverb of place, as you say: "put it aside," and "walk aside." The reading of whoever read "suf-han" with a dammah supports this. In this reading there is another aspect, which is that it be a lightened form of "suhuf", the plural of "sahif", and be in the accusative as a circumstantial, i.e., turning away and averting. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "safhan", its accusative is like the accusative of "sun'a Allah" (the work of God). End of quote. He means that it is a verbal noun emphasising the content of the preceding sentence, so the governing element is omitted; but what he said does not appear to be the case, for its accusative is not like the accusative of "sun'a Allah." Nafi' and al-Akhawan read "in" with a kasrah on the hamzah, yet their transgressing was certain. How, then, does the conditional "in" enter upon it, which only enters upon what is not certain, or upon what is certain but whose time is indefinite? Al-Zamakhshari said: It is of the type of condition that I mentioned as issuing from one who is confident in the correctness of the matter, certain of its establishment, as a hired worker says: "If I have worked for you, then pay me my due," while he knows that, but he gives the impression in his speech that your neglect in departing from the right is the act of one who has doubt about the entitlement, despite its clarity, to make him appear ignorant. Al-Jumhur read "an" with a fathah on the hamzah, meaning: "because you were." The poet said:
"Do you lament that the departing companion has gone?"
Zayd ibn 'Ali read "idh kuntum" with a dhal in place of the nun, when He mentioned an address to the Quraysh: "Shall We turn away from you the Reminder?" This denial was evidence of their denial of the Messenger and a denial of what he had brought. God comforted him by informing him that their habit was the habit of the earlier nations, mocking the messengers, and that God destroyed those who were more mighty in strength than Quraysh, that is, greater in number, in equipment and in stamina.
"And the example of the former peoples has passed": that is, let Quraysh beware lest there befall them the like of what befell the former peoples who denied the messengers, of punishment. This was said by Qatadah: it is the punishment which travelled as a proverb. It is also said: the example of the former peoples in disbelief and denial, and Quraysh had taken their path; the address to them in His words "Shall We turn away from you" had been directed, then He turned from them to report in the third person in His words: "So We destroyed those who were more mighty than them in strength." (And if you ask them): this is an argument against Quraysh with what necessitates contradiction, namely their acknowledgement that the creator of the upper and lower worlds is God, yet they take idols as gods besides God, worshipping and magnifying them. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: the requirement of the answer is that they should say "God created them," but when God mentioned the meaning, the expression about God came as "the Mighty, the Knowing", so that this would be a preparation for the attributes He enumerated, whose announcement He began and which He detached from the speech whose meaning He related from Quraysh. End of quote. Al-Zamakhshari said: they would attribute the creation of them to the One whose attributes these are, and they would ascribe it to Him. End of quote. The apparent meaning is that "the Mighty, the Knowing created them" is the very speech reported from them, and the fact that they mention "God created them" in one place does not prevent them from saying in another question: "The Mighty, the Knowing created them."

"Who made for you": is part of God's speech, addressed to them, reminding them of His previous blessings. He repeated the verb in the answer in His words: "the Mighty, the Knowing created them," for emphasis. In places other than a question, they confined themselves to mentioning the name of God, since He is the proper name comprising the lofty attributes, and the answer corresponds to the question in meaning, not in wording, because "man" is a subject. If it corresponded in wording, it would be with the noun as subject, not with the verb. "So that you may be guided": that is, to your destinations in travel, or that you may be guided by reflection and consideration. "In measure": that is, by decree and determination from eternity, or by sufficiency, not so much that it corrupts, nor so little that it does not avail.

"Then We revived": that is, We gave life by it.
"A dead land": it is mentioned in terms of the rain, and "land" (baldah) is a collective noun. Abu Ja'far and 'Isa read "mayyitan" with a shaddah. Al-Jumhur read "tukhrajun" as passive, while Ibn Wathhab, 'Abd Allah ibn Jubayr al-Mus'bih, 'Isa, Ibn 'Amir and al-Akhawan read it as active. "Al-azwaj": the kinds of everything. It is said: everything other than God is a pair (zawj), like above and below, right and left, front and back, past and future, essences and attributes, summer and winter, spring and autumn. That they are pairs indicates that they are possible in existence, and it indicates that their Originator is single, namely God, exalted above opposites, counterparts and rivals. End of quote.

"And the cattle": the known thing is that only camels are ridden among the cattle. "Ma" is a relative pronoun, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e., what they ride. "Rakiba" is used in relation to causes, and it takes the object directly, while it takes it through "fi" in the sense of the implied "ma yarkabunahu." The lam in "li-tastawu" (so that you may sit firmly): the apparent reading is that it is the lam of purpose. Al-Hawfi said: whoever affirms the lam of becoming may also say so here. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: it is the lam of command, but there is a distance here because of using the imperative of the addressee with the ta of address, which is so rare that it should not be analogised. The eloquent and common form is "idrib," and it is said "li-tadrib"; indeed the grammarians stated that it is a bad and rare dialect, hardly known except as an irregular reading. Therefore, with it, "fal-tafrahu" is read with the ta for address. What the traditionists transmitted from his words, peace be upon him, "li-ta'khudhu masaffakum" (take your ranks), though there is a possibility that the narrator related it by meaning, and the saying of the poet:
"Let you stand, O son of the best of Quraysh, so that you may fulfil the needs of the Muslims."
Al-Zajjaj claimed that it is a good dialect, but this contradicts what the grammarians claimed. The pronoun in "zuhurihi" returns to "ma", as if he said: "on the backs of what you ride," as Abu 'Ubaydah said; hence the plural was appropriate, because its consequence is both word and meaning. Whoever uses the plural does so with regard to meaning, and whoever uses the singular with regard to wording; and what is meant is "of the ships and the cattle." Al-Farra' said something similar, saying: he attributed the backs to them. "Then you may remember" (thumma tadhkaru): that is, in your hearts, "the blessing of your Lord," acknowledging it and magnifying it. He does not mean remembrance by the tongue but by the heart; for this reason He set against it His words: "and say: Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us." That is, glorify God by explicit speech. It has come in a hadith that when he, peace be upon him, put his foot in the stirrup he would say: "In the name of God," and when he settled upon the mount he would say: "Praise be to God for every state; glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and to Him we are returning," and he would say "Allahu akbar" three times and "La ilaha illa Allah" three times. They also said: when one boards a ship he says: "In the name of God is its course and its anchorage" up to "Merciful," and at disembarking one says: "O God, cause us to alight at a blessed landing place, for You are the best of those who cause to alight."

"Qarn" (ability): the one who is dominant, controlling, capable of a thing; it is said: "aqrana al-shay'," when he was able to manage it. Ibn Hermah said:
"You have made able what you laid upon me, and little is it that endurance bears the rejection and the forsaking, O Da'd."
The literal sense of "aqranahu" is that he found it a counterpart to himself, and that which is bound to it. For the difficult does not become a counterpart to the weak. The poet said:
"And the son of the camel-colt, when he is tied with a rope, cannot withstand the charge of the stout, long-necked camels."
"Qarn" is also the rope with which something is tied. Abu 'Ubayd said: "Fulan muqrin li-fulan," meaning he controls him. The meaning is that we have no strength to control the beast and the ship; it is God who subjected them. Qutrub recited for 'Amr ibn Ma'dikarib:
"Indeed the tribes know that 'Aqil, in our favour in the calamities, is not one who subdues us."
It was also read "lamuqtarinin," the active participle of "iqtarana."

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 43, verse 1–18 (part 3 of 3):

﴿And indeed, to our Lord we are returning﴾: i.e., returning (raji'un). This is an affirmation of the return to Allah and of the Resurrection (al-ba'th), because the rider is in a position of possible destruction by drowning when he boards a ship, and by being thrown from a mount, since riding an animal is a matter fraught with danger, and safety in it is not assured. So his saying this is a reminder that he is conscious of the eventual return to Allah and prepared to meet Him, and he does not leave that from his heart or his tongue.

﴿And they have made for Him﴾: i.e., the disbelievers of Quraysh and the Arabs have made for Him, i.e., for Allah, (min 'ibadihi) of His servants: i.e., from among those who are the servants of Allah, (juz'an), a portion. Mujahid said: a share and a lot, and this is the saying of the Arabs: "The angels are the daughters of Allah." Qatadah said: juz'an, i.e., a rival (nid), and that is the idols, Pharaoh, and whoever was worshipped besides Allah. It was also said: al-juz' means females. Some of the linguists said: it is said "ajza'at al-mar'ah" when she gives birth to a female. The poet said:
"If a free woman bears a female one day, there is no wonder, for a free woman sometimes bears a male."
It was said: this verse is fabricated, and likewise his saying:
"He married her to one of the daughters of al-Aws, one who bears females."

Since it had been mentioned that they acknowledge that He, the Exalted, is the Creator of the world, He rebuked them for making for Him a part, while they have acknowledged that He is the Creator. How then do they describe Him with an attribute of the created? ﴿Indeed, man is clearly ungrateful﴾ for the blessing of his Creator. (mubin): manifest in his denial. What is meant by "man" is the one who makes for Allah a part, and others among the disbelievers. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "mubin" in this place is intransitive. End of quote. It is not necessarily restricted to what he mentioned; rather, its meaning may be that it is apparent in ingratitude for blessings and manifest in his denial, as we have said.

﴿Has He taken daughters from what He creates?﴾: an interrogative of denial and rebuke for the scantiness of their intellects. How did they claim that He, the Exalted, took for Himself what you yourselves hate, when you yourselves, when news of them is brought to you, your faces darken, and you bury them alive? (wa-asfakum): He made for you the choicest of what is beloved, and that is sons. His saying (min ma yakhluqu) is an alert to the impossibility of offspring, whether male or female; and even if the taking of offspring is supposed, how would He choose for Himself the lesser and reserve the higher for you? He mentioned the daughters first because they are the ones being denied against them, by attributing them to Allah, and He defined the sons (al-banin) rather than the daughters, as an honouring of them over the daughters.

﴿And when one of them is given good news﴾: the explanation of its counterpart has already been given in Surat al-Nahl.

﴿Or one who is brought up in adornment﴾: i.e., he moves through his life state by state in ornament (al-hilyah), which is jewelry that is suitable only for females and not for males, because they adorn themselves with it for their husbands. And he, if he disputes, does not make clear, due to weakness of intellect and lack of reflection and contemplation; by this he showed their rights and the superiority of sons over them. In this there is an indication that it is not fitting for a man to adorn himself as a woman does, and that he should be rough. The stallion among men refuses to take on the attributes of women. The apparent meaning is that by "one who is brought up in adornment" He meant women. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: and this is indicated by His saying: ﴿while in dispute he is not clear﴾: i.e., he does not produce proof, nor establish evidence, nor reveal what is in his mind in a clear manner. It is said: you rarely find a woman who does not spoil speech and mix up meanings, to the extent that it was reported of some people that he said: "When we enter upon so-and-so, we do not leave until we know that her intellect is the intellect of a woman." Ibn Zayd said: what is meant by "one who is brought up in adornment" is idols, for they used to make many of them from gold and silver, and place jewelry on many of them. This view is weakened by His saying: ﴿while in dispute he is not clear﴾, unless by negating clarity is meant negating dispute, i.e., there is no dispute from them, for it is like His saying:
"Over a well-trodden path whose landmark does not guide one."
i.e., there is no landmark for it so that one might be guided by it. "Man" (man) is in the accusative position, i.e., and they made for Him those who are brought up. It is permissible that it be in the nominative position by way of the inchoative, i.e., whoever is brought up, they made for Allah. The majority read yunasha'u (is brought up) in the active voice; al-Jahdari in one report read it in the passive voice, lightened; Ibn 'Abbas, Zayd ibn 'Ali, al-Hasan, Mujahid, al-Jahdari in one narration, al-Akhawan (the two brothers), Hafs, al-Mufaddal, Aban, Ibn Miqsam and Harun, from Abu 'Amr: in the passive voice, intensified; and al-Hasan in one narration: yunasha'u on the pattern of yufa'alu, in the passive voice, and al-munasha'ah means the same as al-insha', like al-mu'alah means al-i'la'. "In disputation" (fi al-khisam) is connected to an omitted element whose explanation is "not clear," i.e., and he does not make clear in disputation. Whoever permits "amma zaydan ghayru daribin" by making the object of "ghayr" operate, permits that it be connected to "mubin," treating "ghayr" as "la." The placing of the complement of "amma" after "la" is a matter of disagreement, and this has been mentioned in grammar.

[p. 2]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat al-Zukhruf: eighty-nine verses, Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

[p. 3]

﴿Ha Mim.﴾ ﴿By the Book that makes things clear,﴾ ﴿indeed We have made it an Arabic Qur'an, that you may understand.﴾ ﴿And indeed it is, in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and wise.﴾ ﴿Shall We withhold the Reminder from you and turn away from you, because you are a people who transgress?﴾ ﴿How many a prophet did We send among the earlier peoples?﴾ ﴿Yet no prophet came to them but they mocked him.﴾ ﴿So We destroyed those who were stronger than these in might, and the example of the earlier peoples has passed on.﴾ ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "The Mighty, the All-Knowing created them."﴾ ﴿Who made the earth for you as a cradle and made for you therein roads, that you may be guided.﴾ ﴿And who sends down water from the sky in measure, and We revive with it a dead land. Thus you will be brought forth.﴾ ﴿And who created all the pairs and made for you ships and cattle on which you ride,﴾ ﴿that you may sit firmly upon their backs and then remember the favour of your Lord when you are settled upon them, and say, "Glory be to Him who has subjected these to us, and we could not have subdued them ourselves.﴾ ﴿And indeed to our Lord we will return."﴾ ﴿And they have attributed to Him a portion of His servants. Indeed, mankind is clearly ungrateful.﴾ ﴿Has He taken daughters from what He creates and chosen sons for you?﴾ ﴿And when one of them is given news of what he attributes to the Most Gracious, his face darkens, and he is suppressed with grief.﴾ ﴿Is one who is raised in ornament, and who in dispute is not clear?﴾ ﴿And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Gracious, into females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned.﴾ [43:19] ﴿And they say, "If the Most Gracious had willed, we would not have worshipped them." They have no knowledge of that; they only guess.﴾ [43:20] ﴿Did We give them a Book before this, so that they hold fast to it?﴾ [43:21] ﴿Rather, they say, "We found our fathers following a religion, and we are guided by their footsteps."﴾ [43:22] ﴿And thus We did not send a warner before you to any town except that its affluent people said, "We found our fathers following a religion, and we follow in their footsteps."﴾ [43:23] ﴿He said, "Even if I bring you better guidance than what you found your fathers following?" They said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with."﴾ [43:24] ﴿So We took retribution from them. Then see how was the end of the deniers.﴾ [43:25] ﴿And when Abraham said to his father and his people, "Indeed, I am free of what you worship,﴾ [43:26] ﴿except He who originated me, for He will guide me."﴾ [43:27] ﴿And he made it a lasting word among his descendants, that they might return.﴾ [43:28] ﴿Rather, I gave enjoyment to these people and their fathers until the truth and a clear messenger came to them.﴾ [43:29] ﴿And when the truth came to them they said, "This is magic, and we disbelieve in it."﴾ [43:30] ﴿And they said, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from the two cities?"﴾ [43:31] ﴿Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord? We have distributed among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others in rank, that some may take others in service. But the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate.﴾ [43:32] ﴿And were it not that people would become one community, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Gracious roofs of silver for their houses and staircases by which they ascend,﴾ [43:33] ﴿and doors for their houses and couches on which they recline,﴾ [43:34] ﴿and ornaments of gold. But all that is merely the enjoyment of the life of this world, while the Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous.﴾ [43:35] ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Gracious, We appoint for him a devil, and he is his companion.﴾ [43:36] ﴿And indeed they hinder them from the way, while they think they are guided.﴾ [43:37] ﴿Until, when he comes to Us, he says, "Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! What an evil companion!"﴾ [43:38] ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you did wrong, that you will be sharers in the punishment.﴾ [43:39] ﴿Can you, then, make the deaf hear, or guide the blind and those who are in clear error?﴾ [43:40] ﴿And whether We take you away, indeed We will take retribution from them,﴾ [43:41] ﴿or We show you that which We promised them, indeed We are Able over them.﴾ [43:42] ﴿So hold fast to what has been revealed to you. Indeed, you are upon a straight path.﴾ [43:43] ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people, and you will be questioned.﴾ [43:44] ﴿And ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Gracious?﴾ [43:45] ﴿And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, and he said, "Indeed, I am a messenger of the Lord of the worlds."﴾ [43:46] ﴿But when he brought them Our signs, at once they laughed at them.﴾ [43:47] ﴿And We did not show them a sign except that it was greater than its companion, and We seized them with punishment that they might return.﴾ [43:48] ﴿And they said, "O magician, invoke your Lord for us by what He has promised you. Indeed, we will be guided."﴾ [43:49] ﴿But when We removed the punishment from them, at once they broke their word.﴾ [43:50] ﴿And Pharaoh proclaimed among his people, saying, "O my people, is not the kingdom of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me? Do you not see?﴾ [43:51] ﴿Am I not better than this one who is contemptible and can hardly express himself?﴾ [43:52] ﴿Why then have bracelets of gold not been cast upon him, or angels not come with him in succession?"﴾ [43:53] ﴿So he made light of his people, and they obeyed him.
